newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Blue Circle sees potential stg hit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Blue Circle sees potential stg hit.

text.p: Blue Circle Industries Plc, the UK building materials group, said on Monday that if the pound remained at current high levels it could knock 5-10 million stg off pre-tax profits.

James Loudon, finance director, told Reuters in an interview: "Sterling had a minor impact in 1996. But this year may be a different story. If sterling remains at this level it will wipe five to 10 million off profits before tax."
The group has sizeable earnings from both continental Europe and the U.S..
Blue Circle is the latest in a line of UK exporters to issue a warning shot on the strength of sterling.

Commenting on the tough European market conditions seen last year, Loudon said it was unclear when France and Germany would see a pick-up. "In general demand is flat," he said, but added that the demand for boilers in these markets and the UK showed signs of an uptick.
"In the UK we have seen boiler demand up by 10-11 percent last year which has continued into 1997." He added that radiator sales should also be given a kick-start as the UK housing market recovers.

The progress in heating is set to continue after the completion of the first stage of restructuring. The next phase is still to be cleared, he said. Heating will see the loss of 1,300 to 1,400 jobs in total, with 900 redundancies made to date.
The heavy building materials business was broadly ahead, apart from the UK and Chile.
Loudon said that the UK market had suffered from a four percent fall in cement demand. "Although our volumes were down less than that," said the finance chief.
But he said demand had improved since the results and was currently up by around two percent on last year and is seen maintaining that level through 1997.

The problems in the Chile cement unit was due to softening of prices, he said. "But that business is still making extremely good returns on capital employed. Prices in Chile could soften a little and will probably stabilise, but we're doubful of any kind of price increase."
The group plans to fuel the momentum for organic growth in building materials worldwide through heavy capital expenditure.
It has already announced plans for 300 million of investment in the UK over the next five years and further capital expenditure in the U.S. and Chile.
That five year programme totals at 500 million on top of regular replacement spending of around 100 million a year he said, taking the total to one billion of investment over five years.

But he added "We still have scope for further acquisitions." Blue Circle is interested in expansion in the U.S., and Far East markets like Indonesia and Thailand, India and South America, citing Argentina in particular.
